title: Contenta In Hoc Volvmine. Pimander. Mercurij Trismegisti liber de de sapientia et potestate dei. Asclepius ... Crater Hermetis A Lazarelo Septempedano
shelf_note: Lefèvre d'Étaples' 1505 Paris edition of Ficino's Pimander with commentary: core Hermetica. It has no collection assigned. The catalogue title also carries the typo 'de de sapientia'.
structure_note: The book is foliated: only rectos carry a number ('16', '17'), so 78 of 164 pages have a printed number. The 12 backsteps and 17 repeats most likely come from the leaf-numbering scheme and misread numerals, not from a splice. The three sampled pages run in order. OCR and translation are complete.

ocr_errors.problem: 'insunt essentia' (in this essence) misread as 'sunt effeta'
passive abbreviation (inquinatur) dropped, so the sense turns active

tr_errors.source: Inquinat[ur] enim hoc bonum admixtione malorum. infectum vero ulterius bonum non permanet, sin minime permanet: malum efficit[ur]
tr_errors.english: For this good pollutes with the admixture of evils; the good, however, does not remain further infected. If it does not remain at all, it makes evil.
tr_errors.problem: The argument is garbled. The source says this good is polluted by evil, once infected it no longer stays good, and if it does not stay good it becomes evil. The translation inverts the agency and the logic, following the OCR misreads.

tr_errors.source: Quare solum boni nomen homini adest o Esculapi
tr_errors.english: Wherefore, let the name of the good be present to man alone, O Asclepius
tr_errors.problem: The statement that only the NAME of good belongs to man becomes a jussive, and 'solum' is misattached to 'man'

tr_errors.english: none of those things that are evil are contained in Him
tr_errors.problem: 'in this essence' rendered as 'in Him'; recoverable

book_verdict: The text is the right leaves and readable. Contraction-heavy roman type causes misexpansions that the flash-lite translation carries into fluent but wrong philosophy: one passage on p31 garbles Hermes' argument that good, once mixed with evil, becomes evil. The book is usable, but a careful reader of the Hermetica would catch errors.

title: Claudian, Opera (Aldine Press)
shelf_note: Aldine 1523 Claudian in early-european-books; a classical poet, fine for that collection.
structure_note: Leaf numbers appear only on rectos (p112 shows '30'), so the 41 backsteps and 34 repeats are probably numeral misreads or leaf-numbering, not a splice. The pages_translated field (356) is stale against the 372 pages counted as translated.

tr_errors.english: The court is empty of dances and feasts
tr_errors.problem: Sense inverted. 'vacat' + ablative here means the court has leisure for (is given over to) dances and feasts while the empire burns, so the satire is reversed.

tr_errors.english: The rising expanse will grow foul, the plows having been driven out.
tr_errors.problem: 'oriens' is the East, which will lie waste more widely; 'rising expanse' is meaningless

tr_errors.source: quas urbes, & quanto tempore Martis / Ignaras uno rapuerunt prælia cursu
tr_errors.english: what cities, and in what time of Mars, / Ignorant of war, they have seized
tr_errors.problem: Should read 'cities so long ignorant of war'; 'quanto tempore' is misconstrued

tr_errors.source: Præda sumus iam Bistoniis, Hæmoque niuali
tr_errors.english: Are to the Bistones and the snowy tribes
tr_errors.problem: Haemus (the mountain) rendered as 'snowy tribes'

ocr_errors.image: guide letter 'e' beside the unprinted initial of 'Continuant'

tr_errors.source: Continuant superi pleno Romana fauore gaudia
tr_errors.english: May the gods continue the Roman joys
tr_errors.problem: indicative statement rendered as a wish

tr_errors.english: the axes of the consul rise up, defended by Stilicho
tr_errors.problem: Should read 'with Stilicho as consul, the fasces he defended rise'; minor misconstrual

other.note: OCR stores a model description ('The text is printed in an italic typeface with upright capital initials. There is some bleed-through...') in a <meta> tag
Centering arrows '->...<-' in the OCR around the opening lines

ocr_errors.problem: 'An gelidam' (or shall I sing of icy Thrace) fused into a pseudo-name

tr_errors.english: It will be meager.
tr_errors.problem: Sense reversed. The poet says whatever he leaves out will be GREATER; the translation invents 'meager' from the misread.

tr_errors.source: An gelidam Thracem, decertatosque labores / Hebro teste canam?
tr_errors.english: Shall I sing of the Thracian Angelida
tr_errors.problem: Invented person 'Angelida' from the OCR fusion

tr_errors.source: cuius protendere famam ... Sufficeret natus Stilico
tr_errors.english: Whose fame ... would be enough for his son Stilicho
tr_errors.problem: Should read 'his son Stilicho alone would suffice to spread his fame'; the relation is inverted

book_verdict: The OCR of the Aldine italic is very good. The lite translation of Claudian's verse, though, makes sense-reversing errors on two of three pages ('the court is empty of feasts'; 'it will be meager'), and an invented 'Angelida' follows an OCR fusion. A Latinist would notice these at once.

title: Schat der Gesontheyt
shelf_note: Early modern medicine by Beverwijck fits early-european-books. The catalogue record, however, does not describe this scan (see structure_note).
structure_note: Catalogue identity looks wrong (I7). The record says 'Schat der Gesontheyt', language Dutch, but every sampled page is Latin, with running heads 'THERAPEVTICE.' / 'MED. VET. PARS III.' and Latin chapter heads (Cap. II on plague). This looks like Beverwijck's Latin 'Idea medicinae veterum' (Leiden, 1637), not the Dutch Schat der Gesontheyt (identification inferred from the running heads; not verified against the title page). Printed numbering 193-195 is continuous; the 5 backsteps are probably misread numerals.

tr_errors.source: Ita Gallus, siue Pythagoras ... Lucian. Gallo.
tr_errors.english: Thus the Gaul, or Pythagoras ... Lucian, The Gaul.
tr_errors.problem: Lucian's dialogue is 'The Cock' (Gallus, the rooster who was once Pythagoras); 'the Gaul' is wrong

tr_errors.source: Non igitur imitari debemus bonos naviculatores
tr_errors.english: we must not imitate good sailors
tr_errors.problem: acceptable; the irony of 'bonos' is flattened

other.note: Translation field ends with <summary>…</summary> and <keywords>…</keywords> blocks; they are a leak if the reader does not strip them

tr_errors.source: non dandum in febre, nisi veteribus ægris, vinum
tr_errors.english: wine should not be given in a fever, except to aged patients
tr_errors.problem: 'veteres aegri' are long-standing (chronic) patients, not the aged; a dosing rule is misstated

tr_errors.english: you declaim with a double tertian <note>a fever recurring every other day</note>
tr_errors.problem: hemitritaeus is a semi-tertian fever, so both the translation and the added gloss are wrong

ocr_errors.problem: long-s read as f in the italic heading but as ſ in the body

tr_errors.english: phoinios nosos — blood-red disease
tr_errors.problem: Carries the OCR substitution; Sophocles' phrase is 'bloody surge'

book_verdict: The OCR and translation of the pages are good, with a few moderate slips (chronic vs aged patients, 'the Gaul'). The book's identity is the problem: it is catalogued as the Dutch 'Schat der Gesontheyt', but the scan is a Latin 'Medicina veterum' work by the same author. A reader sees that mismatch at once.

title: De Memoria Artificiosa Libellus
shelf_note: Magirus' 1603 art-of-memory catechism fits the library's early modern knowledge remit and early-european-books.
structure_note: Printed pages 15-17 run in order and the single backstep is negligible. 5 of 54 pages are untranslated.

tr_errors.english: large, incredible, ugly, unheard of
tr_errors.problem: 'inuisae' paired with 'inauditae' means unseen, not ugly

ocr_errors.problem: catchword placed in the body as centred text (also in meta)

tr_errors.english: Voices are likewise twofold
tr_errors.problem: 'voces' here means words

other.note: Running head 'DE ARTE' turned into an invented H1 heading '# ON THE ART'
Empty centring arrows '-><-' left at the end of the translation (catchword removed, markup kept)
Running head 'REMINISCENTIÆ.' rendered as an invented H1 heading '# REMINISCENCES.'

book_verdict: Clean OCR and a largely faithful translation; one word ('inuisae' as 'ugly') is wrong. Running heads promoted to headings ('ON THE ART', 'REMINISCENCES.') and a stray '-><-' are visible blemishes.

title: Disputatio 20. De obligationlbus, quae quasi ex contractu nascuntur ...
shelf_note: A 13-page Helmstedt (Academia Julia) student disputation on Roman-law quasi-contract (negotiorum gestio, tutela). It is a genuine early modern print but far from the library's core traditions and has no collection. The catalogue title also has the typo 'obligationlbus'.
structure_note: 13 pages, all OCR'd and translated, with no printed page numbers (signatures only), which matches a short disputation.

tr_errors.problem: The legal sense is that the gestor is sometimes liable even for accident (casus); 'provided for' obscures it

tr_errors.problem: Title of D.3.5 means 'on business managed'; recurring

ocr_errors.problem: citation garbled ('&' read as '5'); small type, low confidence

tr_errors.english: the said Law 8
tr_errors.problem: Invented law number '8' in the citation (neither image 5 nor OCR 's.')

tr_errors.source: in duplum cui rei persecutio inest, tenetur
tr_errors.english: is held for double, to which is added the prosecution of the thing itself
tr_errors.problem: The double INCLUDES recovery of the thing (actio mixta); 'is added' states the opposite legal rule

book_verdict: OCR and translation are serviceable for a dense legal disputation. The OCR expands sigla silently, the translation mangles a few legal technicalities and one citation number, and '<note>original: "x"</note>' clutter repeats throughout. It is on the margin of the library's scope.
